messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — high error rate on serving-prod (CUDA_ILLEGAL). Priority: P1. Detected 20 node-level OOM+CUDA illegal memory access events in the last 3m. Paging symptoms and container restarts observed. Pager: @samir

samir: joining now. saw the same alerts, tailing logs. nodes: gpu-pool-2a (4/8), gpu-pool-2b (6/8) showing repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` and kernel tracebacks.

tara: on it. I’ll grab controller logs and the runtime metrics. Is there a customer impact snapshot?

patrick: support sees spikes in 500s from customers using embedding/long-context endpoints. ~12% request failure rate for the last 10m, affecting both hosted and some Dedicated customers in eu-west. Posting list to #customer-success shortly.

ops-bot: auto-runbook attached: /runbooks/CUDA_ILLEGAL.md — suggested mitigations: isolate nodes, fallback to smaller model variant, disable reuse-kv-cache.

yvette: what kernel/driver versions on those nodes? looks like we just rolled nvidia-driver-530.41 last night in 2a. 2b is still on 525.

samir: confirmed — 2a = nvidia/530.41, 2b = nvidia/525.85. Weird that both pools are failing. stack traces show `misaligned address` from pagewalk in the GPU driver.

derek: attaching a snippet from container stdout (repro log):
```
2026-03-15T10:22:07Z runtime: CUDA illegal memory access at 0x7f8c3a2b
kworker/3:2 [error] pagewalk: unaligned pte access at va=0x7ffc5f.., pc=0xffffffff
Container restart (OOM)  status=137
```

patrick: customers asking for ETA. we should call out mitigations ASAP.

samir: immediate plan: 1) cordon affected nodes in gpu-pool-2a/2b; 2) drain critical serving pods off suspect GPUs; 3) fallback routing: route new requests to cpu-backup pool or smaller-quantized model variants; 4) rollback driver to 525 on 2a as quick test; 5) enable debug capture & memory sanitizer on one node for postmortem.

tara: executing cordon/drain now for node gpu-2a-12 and gpu-2b-07.

ops-bot: Command executed by tara: `kubectl cordon gpu-2a-12 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-2a-12`

alice: adding priority list of customers impacted. We should prepare an incident notification draft for customers on hosted API and Dedicated accounts. Include workaround: use region us-east or cpu fallbacks.

samir: doing the driver rollback test on a single node (gpu-2a-12): switching from 530.41 -> 525.85. will restart kubelet after driver swap.

yvette: heads up — kernel patch we tried last month (pagewalk alignment guard) may be relevant. I'll pull kernel oops from dmesg and compare.

derek: note — models with long context and KV-cache-heavy workloads spike memory usage, might expose a kernel race during eviction. Suggest also temporarily reducing max_sequence_length on hosted model routes to limit KV cache size.

patrick: draft notice to customers: "We are investigating an issue causing intermittent CUDA errors and container restarts for some GPU-backed endpoints. Immediate workaround: route traffic to CPU fallback models or smaller model variants in alternate regions. We will update shortly." Should we send now?

samir: hold on public message until we confirm rollback outcome. If rollback fixes illegal access on test node, we can start a controlled rollback across the pool. If not, we'll do routing fallback first.

ops-bot: node gpu-2a-12 driver rollback completed. kubelet restarted. Monitoring logs.

(t+3m) tara: test node logs show no `CUDA illegal memory access` events since restart — reduced error rate for pods that were moved off the node.

samir: good sign. still see errors on other nodes (esp gpu-2b-07) — not all failures are driver-version specific. Could be a race triggered by certain eviction/page sequences.

yvette: starting a phased rollback of driver on gpu-pool-2a only (3 nodes at a time) while we keep gpu-pool-2b throttled. Will coordinate with infra to avoid disruption.

derek: enabling reduced model-length on a canary set of routes now: set `max_tokens=2048` by config patch to reduce KV memory.

ops-bot: deploy started: service=runtime-canary, sha=def456, rollout=10% -> 100% (estimated 7m).

patrick: support note — some customers on Dedicated required a manual restart of their dedicated replica; ops is contacting the account owners and offering a rollback window.

alice: we should capture a proof-of-impact metric for SLA/credits: collecting 5m aggregated error rate before/after mitigation.

samir: quick status: cordoned 6 nodes, driver rollback in progress on 4 nodes, routing fallback enabled for 15% of traffic to cpu-backup, KV-cache disabled for 10% of canary traffic, customer-facing notice draft ready pending approval.

(t+8m) tara: small regression observed during driver swap on node gpu-2a-14 — kubelet OOMed due to large graceful termination load; I restarted the node and increased eviction thresholds.

ops-bot: ALERT: node-flap detected: gpu-2a-14 rebooted unexpectedly. Auto-recover sequence initiated.

samir: we need to watch for cascading node flaps — adjust replacement autoscaling to avoid bringing new pods onto suspect hardware until validated. Setting nodeSelector to prefer untouched pools.

derek: collected coredump and driver trace from one failing container — uploading to artifact store. Will share link.

(t+20m) tara: after rolling rollback across 2a, error rate for routes on 2a dropped from 12%->1.5%. 2b still 10%+.

yvette: 2b investigation: those nodes also show high DMA remap pagewalk retries. NVIDIA driver didn't cause all failures. I'm opening kernel oops ticket with vendor. Meanwhile we'll keep rollback across 2b as well but slower.

patrick: customer-impact update: currently ~6% global request failure (down from 12%), affected tenants list sent to CS. No data leakage reported. Most failures are transient 5xx, not silent corruption.

alice: publish customer update now with suggested workarounds and ETA for next update in 30m. Approved.

ops-bot: NOTIFICATION SENT to affected customers (hosted/dedicated subset).

samir: next steps: 1) finish driver rollback on 2b with careful pacing, 2) run stress test on one patched node with memory-sanitizer, 3) capture live NVidia and kernel traces for vendor. Create postmortem template and set SEV follow-up meeting for 2h.

derek: adding mitigations list to thread for postmortem: - driver rollback 530->525 (partial fix), - reduced model context length to limit KV cache, - temporary routing to cpu-backup, - cordon/drain for suspect nodes, - increased eviction headroom during maintenance.

(t+60m) tara: handing off to oncall for long-term recovery. samir still on call for vendor coordination.

samir: handing off to week-oncall @yvette for follow-up and root-cause. leaving notes in the incident doc.

yvette: acknowledged. I'll own vendor engagement and kernel oops triage. setting follow-up meeting.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status: mitigated (error rate reduced to acceptable threshold). Follow-ups scheduled: kernel vendor debug, long-term hardening (hotpatch guard), improved telemetry on pagewalk alignment, and a remediation runbook update.

patrick: final customer note scheduled for 2h with timeline and credits info.

alice: thanks team. good coordination. please capture all timelines and commands in the postmortem.

samir: thanks all — closing our P1 shift handoff.
